key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205, a longer spray distance of 190 mm produced the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance in acidic conditions.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical process lever for improving coating compactness and extending corrosion protection of stainless-steel components in aggressive industrial acid environments.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm
Tested electrochemical behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization
Compared microstructure and porosity using SEM
evidence_signal: Porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating had the lowest corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate.
watch_item: The result is specific to 1 M H2SO4 at room temperature, so performance should be validated under other acids, temperatures, and service conditions before deployment.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
